title: BR-046 intake: CBSP21 gate names an unrelated stale manifest when nothing covers the diff (queue entry only)
intent: Files a bounded, CI-reproduced diagnostic defect surfaced by the DEP-SEC-001B negative-gate witness during PR #259 review. When no manifest declares any changed file, CBSP21 auto-discovery still selects a manifest (an arbitrary stale one from a merged PR) and prints it as the manifest at 0.0% coverage, misdirecting the reader away from the real cause: no per-PR manifest has been written. Queue entry only — this patch defines scope and does not repair the tooling.
behavior_change: None. Documentation only - two governance records gain an entry. No CI script, workflow, gate threshold, manifest-discovery logic, or production source is modified. The CBSP21 gate behaves identically before and after this patch.

diff_articulation.what_changed: Adds a new 'Tooling-diagnostic intake' section to REPOSITORY_DEFECT_REGISTER.md containing BR-046, with verbatim CI output, the governing-contract contradiction, an explicit severity boundary (diagnostic quality only; enforcement unaffected), and a provisional repair direction. Adds the matching BR-046 row plus an evidence-and-boundary note to BACKLOG_ADJUDICATION_LEDGER.md, so the register and ledger agree at intake — deliberately not repeating the BR-037..BR-042 write-back divergence the ledger already records against itself.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No existing BR covers CBSP21 tooling. The nearest neighbours are unrelated: BR-022 is SG_SPEC_TOKEN env-guard rollout, CI-RED-001 is sg-spec clone auth. The behaviour also contradicts a stated contract in .cbsp21/patches/README.md ('stale manifests ... are ignored automatically'), so it is a real inconsistency rather than an undocumented preference.

commands_run: CI reproduction: GitHub Actions run 31466755438 — workflow_dispatch of cbsp21_gate.yml on a throwaway branch off main @ 25fc189d carrying exactly one undeclared file. Conclusion: failure. Output named 'Manifest: .cbsp21/patches/audit-n1-refuted.json' at 0.0% coverage while correctly listing the uncovered file. Witness branch deleted after capture; origin/main unchanged at 25fc189d.

Local control (enforcement is sound, both directions, same manifest): check_cbsp21_gate.py with PR #259's declared 5-file set -> Coverage 100.0%, exit 0. Same set plus one undeclared file (services/api/app/main.py) -> Coverage 80.0%, exit 1, uncovered file named.

Historical corroboration: PRs #251 and #252 both failed this gate reporting 'Manifest: .cbsp21/patches/wp-002-a-shim-reconfirmation.json' at 0.0% coverage; in both cases the true cause was an absent per-PR manifest.
Contract check: .cbsp21/patches/README.md states stale manifests 'are ignored automatically' — read directly on origin/main.
Next-id check: `git grep -oh 'BR-0[0-9][0-9]' origin/main -- docs/remediation/` -> highest existing is BR-045; BR-046 is free.
scripts/ci/check_cbsp21_gate.py and scripts/ci/check_cbsp21_patch_input.py run locally on this branch -> PASS

files.intent: File BR-046 as a CI-reproduced diagnostic defect with an explicit severity boundary separating diagnosis quality from enforcement correctness.
Add the matching BR-046 ledger row at intake so register and ledger do not diverge.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Intake only; no tooling repair is authorized by this patch and the gate is unchanged. The defect is explicitly bounded as diagnostic-quality: the same witness that exposed it proved coverage enforcement correct in both directions, and no PR has been wrongly admitted or rejected. Filed on its own branch rather than folded into PR #259 because adding a tooling fix to a docs/governance patch is precisely the scope contamination SPRINTS_MAINTENANCE Rule 8 and this gate exist to prevent.
